title: Membrane Biochemistry
source_note: Grounded in standard biochemistry curricula on biological membranes (Lehninger, Voet & Voet, Alberts' Molecular Biology of the Cell) covering membrane composition, fluid mosaic model, transport mechanisms, and membrane-associated signaling.

questions.question: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by which scientists?
questions.explanation: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972, describing the membrane as a fluid lipid bilayer with embedded mobile proteins.

questions.question: Which class of membrane lipids is most abundant in mammalian plasma membranes?
questions.explanation: Phosphoglycerides (glycerophospholipids) such as phosphatidylcholine make up the bulk of membrane lipids in most eukaryotic membranes.

questions.question: In a phospholipid bilayer, the hydrophobic fatty acyl tails orient toward each other because they are:
options: Excluded from water by the hydrophobic effect
Attracted to the polar head groups
questions.correct_answer: Excluded from water by the hydrophobic effect
questions.explanation: Amphipathic lipids spontaneously arrange so nonpolar tails avoid water, driven by the hydrophobic effect, forming the bilayer interior.

questions.question: Which membrane component is primarily responsible for modulating membrane fluidity in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Cholesterol intercalates between phospholipids, restraining fluidity at high temperatures and preventing tight packing at low temperatures, acting as a fluidity buffer.

questions.question: Integral membrane proteins differ from peripheral membrane proteins in that integral proteins:
options: Span or embed within the lipid bilayer
Can be removed by simple salt washes
questions.correct_answer: Span or embed within the lipid bilayer
questions.explanation: Integral proteins are embedded in or span the hydrophobic core of the membrane and require detergents to extract, unlike peripheral proteins bound by ionic/polar interactions.

questions.question: The asymmetric distribution of phospholipids between the two leaflets of a membrane is maintained mainly by:
questions.explanation: ATP-dependent flippases and floppases actively translocate specific phospholipids between leaflets, maintaining bilayer asymmetry since spontaneous flip-flop is very slow.

questions.question: Lateral diffusion of lipids within a membrane leaflet occurs:
options: Rapidly, allowing lipids to exchange positions frequently
At the same rate as transverse (flip-flop) movement
Only in the presence of ATP
questions.correct_answer: Rapidly, allowing lipids to exchange positions frequently
questions.explanation: Lateral diffusion of lipids within a leaflet is fast (occurring in microseconds), in contrast to slow spontaneous transbilayer flip-flop movement.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes facilitated diffusion?
options: Movement of a solute down its concentration gradient via a carrier or channel protein, without ATP
Movement of a solute against its concentration gradient using ATP
Bulk movement of fluid through vesicle formation
Movement of water only through the lipid bilayer
questions.correct_answer: Movement of a solute down its concentration gradient via a carrier or channel protein, without ATP
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion uses membrane transport proteins to move solutes down their concentration gradient without direct energy expenditure.

questions.question: The Na+/K+-ATPase pump moves ions across the membrane in which arrangement per cycle?
questions.explanation: The Na+/K+-ATPase hydrolyzes one ATP to pump 3 Na+ ions out of and 2 K+ ions into the cell against their gradients, an example of primary active transport.

questions.question: A transporter that moves two different solutes across a membrane in the same direction is called a(n):
questions.explanation: Symporters co-transport two solutes in the same direction, such as the Na+/glucose symporter, often using the gradient of one solute to drive the other.

questions.question: The Na+/Ca2+ exchanger, which moves Ca2+ out of cells while Na+ enters, is an example of a(n):
questions.explanation: Antiporters move two different solutes in opposite directions across the membrane; the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger uses the inward Na+ gradient to drive Ca2+ efflux.

questions.question: Aquaporins are integral membrane proteins that primarily facilitate the transport of:
questions.explanation: Aquaporins are channel proteins specialized for rapid, selective transport of water molecules across the plasma membrane.

questions.question: Primary active transport differs from secondary active transport in that primary active transport:
options: Directly uses ATP hydrolysis to move solutes against their gradient
Relies on an existing ion gradient established by another pump
Never moves solutes against a concentration gradient
questions.correct_answer: Directly uses ATP hydrolysis to move solutes against their gradient
questions.explanation: Primary active transport directly couples ATP hydrolysis to solute movement, whereas secondary active transport uses the electrochemical gradient created by a primary pump.

questions.question: ABC (ATP-Binding Cassette) transporters are characterized by:
options: Using ATP hydrolysis to transport substrates across membranes
Functioning without any nucleotide binding domains
questions.correct_answer: Using ATP hydrolysis to transport substrates across membranes
questions.explanation: ABC transporters constitute a large family of primary active transporters that bind and hydrolyze ATP to move a wide range of substrates, including drugs and lipids, across membranes.

questions.question: The glycocalyx on the outer surface of the plasma membrane is composed mainly of:
options: Carbohydrate chains attached to lipids and proteins
questions.correct_answer: Carbohydrate chains attached to lipids and proteins
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx consists of oligosaccharide chains of glycoproteins and glycolipids on the extracellular membrane surface, important in cell recognition and adhesion.

questions.question: Lipid rafts in the plasma membrane are microdomains enriched in:
questions.explanation: Lipid rafts are specialized, more ordered membrane microdomains enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids that serve as platforms for signaling protein clustering.

questions.question: Gap junctions between adjacent animal cells function primarily to:
options: Allow direct passage of small molecules and ions between cells
Anchor cells firmly to the extracellular matrix
questions.correct_answer: Allow direct passage of small molecules and ions between cells
questions.explanation: Gap junctions are formed by connexon channels that directly connect the cytoplasm of adjacent cells, permitting passage of ions and small metabolites.

questions.question: Receptor-mediated endocytosis begins with ligand binding followed by:
options: Clustering of receptors in clathrin-coated pits
Immediate lysis of the plasma membrane
Direct diffusion of the ligand through the bilayer
questions.correct_answer: Clustering of receptors in clathrin-coated pits
questions.explanation: In receptor-mediated endocytosis, ligand-bound receptors cluster in clathrin-coated pits that invaginate and pinch off to form coated vesicles.

questions.question: SNARE proteins play a key role in membrane biology by mediating:
options: Lipid synthesis in the endoplasmic reticulum
DNA replication at the nuclear membrane
questions.explanation: SNARE proteins on vesicle and target membranes pair up to catalyze membrane fusion during exocytosis and vesicular trafficking.

questions.question: Osmosis refers to the net movement of:
options: Water across a selectively permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration
Solutes across a membrane against their gradient
questions.correct_answer: Water across a selectively permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the passive movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration.

questions.question: A cell placed in a hypertonic solution will most likely:
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution, the external solute concentration is higher, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis, causing it to shrink or crenate.

questions.question: The resting membrane potential of most animal cells is maintained largely by the differential permeability of the membrane to:
questions.explanation: The resting membrane potential is largely determined by the high resting permeability to K+ and the outward K+ gradient maintained by the Na+/K+-ATPase.

questions.question: The Donnan equilibrium describes the unequal distribution of diffusible ions across a membrane that arises because of:
options: The presence of non-diffusible charged macromolecules on one side
Complete membrane impermeability to all ions
questions.correct_answer: The presence of non-diffusible charged macromolecules on one side
questions.explanation: Donnan equilibrium arises when impermeant charged macromolecules (e.g., proteins) on one side of a membrane cause an unequal distribution of permeant ions to satisfy electroneutrality.

questions.question: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) are characterized structurally by:
questions.explanation: GPCRs have a characteristic seven-transmembrane-helix architecture and couple ligand binding to intracellular heterotrimeric G-protein activation.

questions.question: Which second messenger is generated by adenylate cyclase upon activation of a stimulatory G-protein (Gs)?
questions.explanation: Activated Gs stimulates adenylate cyclase to convert ATP into cAMP, a key second messenger that activates protein kinase A.

questions.question: Phospholipase C hydrolyzes PIP2 to generate which two second messengers?
questions.explanation: Phospholipase C cleaves phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) into IP3, which triggers Ca2+ release, and DAG, which activates protein kinase C.

questions.question: Membrane biogenesis of glycerophospholipids occurs primarily at the:
questions.explanation: Most membrane phospholipid synthesis occurs on the cytosolic face of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, from where lipids are distributed to other organelles.

questions.question: Sphingomyelin, a sphingolipid found in the plasma membrane, contains which backbone instead of glycerol?
questions.explanation: Sphingolipids are built on a sphingosine backbone rather than glycerol, distinguishing them structurally from glycerophospholipids.

questions.question: Which technique is commonly used to experimentally demonstrate lateral diffusion of membrane proteins?
questions.explanation: FRAP bleaches fluorescently labeled membrane proteins in a region and measures fluorescence recovery as unbleached proteins diffuse in, demonstrating lateral mobility.

questions.question: Ion channels differ from carrier proteins in that channels typically:
options: Allow much faster ion flux without significant conformational cycling
Require ATP hydrolysis for every ion transported
Bind their substrate with very high affinity like enzymes
questions.correct_answer: Allow much faster ion flux without significant conformational cycling
questions.explanation: Channels form aqueous pores allowing very rapid ion flow (near diffusion-limited rates), unlike carriers which undergo conformational changes and are comparatively slower.

questions.question: Voltage-gated ion channels open or close in response to:
questions.explanation: Voltage-gated channels contain charged voltage-sensor domains that respond to changes in transmembrane voltage, triggering conformational changes that open or close the pore.

questions.question: The unit membrane concept, an early model preceding the fluid mosaic model, described the membrane as:
options: A single layer of phospholipids only
A random mixture of lipids and proteins with no order
A rigid crystalline lattice of proteins
questions.explanation: The Davson-Danielli unit membrane model proposed a lipid bilayer sandwiched between two continuous layers of protein, later superseded by the fluid mosaic model.

questions.question: Which membrane protein is responsible for glucose uptake by facilitated diffusion in most mammalian cells?
questions.explanation: GLUT (glucose transporter) proteins are uniporters that facilitate glucose movement down its concentration gradient across the plasma membrane.

questions.question: Cell-cell adhesion mediated by calcium-dependent transmembrane glycoproteins is primarily carried out by:
questions.explanation: Cadherins are calcium-dependent adhesion molecules whose extracellular domains mediate homophilic binding between adjacent cells.

questions.question: A patient's red blood cells are placed in distilled water. Based on osmotic principles, the expected outcome is:
options: No change since RBC membranes are impermeable to water
Immediate active pumping of water out
questions.explanation: Distilled water is strongly hypotonic relative to the cell interior, so water rushes into the RBC by osmosis, causing swelling and eventual lysis (hemolysis).

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the lipid bilayer is largely impermeable to ions and large polar molecules?
options: The hydrophobic core repels charged and highly polar species
Ions are too small to be excluded
Polar molecules are covalently bonded to lipids
The bilayer has fixed pores that exclude only water
questions.correct_answer: The hydrophobic core repels charged and highly polar species
questions.explanation: The nonpolar hydrocarbon interior of the bilayer creates a substantial energy barrier for ions and polar solutes, making the membrane selectively permeable and necessitating transport proteins.
